Bo-Kaap Gentrification

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
The residents of Cape Town’s Bo Kaap have been fighting developers for years, the latest is against an apartment/office block in Lion Street when a crane was prevented from entering and some protesters hauled off to jail.
About 50 protesters gathered at the corner of Buiten and Buitengracht Street on Tuesday. Their aim was to prevent a crane from entering Bo-Kaap and making its way to a development on 40 Lion Street.
On at least two occasions, riot police officers forced them out of the street using shields and stun grenades. According to SAPS, four people were arrested.
We look at this age old and historic area of Cape Town and it’s process of gentrification, what does this mean to the people whose families have lived hear. for decades. They are seeing their ancestors mowed down, their communities broken apart as firstly trendy South Africans and tourists bought these quaint houses often at steal - to now developers coming in with multi storey apartment blocks aimed at a lifestyle of people who see the City Bowl and specifically Bo-kaap the place to live.
“These developers don’t care about our people, they don’t care about the culture. The fact that more than 17 generations have lived in some of these houses,”
Bo-Kaap dates back to the 1760s, when rental houses were built and leased to slaves. According to the Heritage Portal, liberated slaves moved into the area after 1834 and with them Malay people who had been living in the town. The community was one of the few inner-city areas where people were not forcibly removed under the Group Areas Act during apartheid.

Script:


V/O
As the call to prayer sounds on this hot Friday afternoon - residents of Bo- Kaap, Cape Town make their way to mosque -it’s a prayer ritual for the Muslim community here, that goes back 300 years.

Paul: You’ve got about 11 mosques in the area that already that should tell you about the importance of Islam.

V/O Tichmann
Paul Tichmann was a curator of the Bo Kaap Museum, the roots of this community go back to 1768.

Paul : Bo Kaap’s story is really related to story of slavery and and story of apartheid. But Bo Kaap started out as a residential area that housed artisans from Europe but also included a number of people referred to as free blacks and the free blacks were actually former slaves, political exiles, for crimes they had committed and at the end of their sentences many came to live here in the Bo Kaap area.

Faldela: Bo Kaap is one of the best places to be.

V/O
Faldela Tolker’s home, right in the centre of Bo kaap, is from where she runs her catering company and hosts cooking classes – Cooking with Love, the Malay way.

Faldela: The community are so fantastic they are there for each other. You know we are open we are giving that is the mentality of the Bo Kaap people we share we give its laughter
Claire It sounds magical.
Faldela: It is.

V/O
Forty year old, Abdul Karder Peterson works at the Malay Museum,

Abdul : “You should come to the Cape Malay Museum….”

V/O
he was born here, grew up here and wants the same life for his children.

Abdul: Paradise life is here, love you get here greeting each other Rugby watching the rugby.

Link: Bo Kaap, these houses, cobbled roads the colours all make it a tourist hub, a bloggers paradise and a photographers dream. But on the trail of this trendiness come developers who want to exploit the area for commercial gain ..the question is at what cost.

V/O
As Bo – Kaap’s popularity has grown, the area has become increasingly hemmed in by high rise development, from trendy apartment bocks, boutique hotels to business’s.

It’s the heritage of Bo Kap that’s under threat, a heritage residents feel the City are doing nothing to protect…Osman Shaboodien is Chairman of the Bo Kaap Civic and Rate Payers Association.

Osman Shaboodien
chairperson  Bo Kaap Civic and Rate Payers Association

The biggest thing we are objecting to is they sold public land to developers without going through the public process under the guise they had the right to do so.

Mohammad: We are talking about unethical developments, developments developments not in line with Bo- kaaps heritage and cultural norms development, that will completely change the face of Bo-Kaap.

V/O. 
For Mohammad Groenewald, it’s a case of David against Goliath.

Mohammad: If a development goes up, the community now has to take city to court and court cases not cheap so the community have to pay double for these kind of cases million rand to fight a court case in the high court
Claire: What if I am a willing seller to a developer are you against that?
Mohammad: We cannot stop that, we need to look at type of development must not be a 30 story home.. BO Kaap old 250 years old.

Link
It is this apartment block that is going up in Lion Street that sparked the protests late last year the residents of Bo Kaap felt that this is the final straw.

20th November 2018
V/O
In a show of force, the protesters tried to prevent a crane from entering Bo Kaap, and making its way to the Lion Street development…………..Chaos Erupted.

V/O
Jacky Poking and her daughter Kirsten were there, fighting for their community.

Jackie and Kirsten
I was holding her like this the came in and they dragged her from Police dragged her from my arms I was running to try and save her…
Kitsten: ..look for my my Mom but she was gone;

Fowzia I kept on saying the struggle is over I don’t have to go back to streets and fight and lo and behold I could never imagine finding myself back on the street.
It is I wanted to cry because for me I was saying is this our democracy we are facing the police like we faced the police in the old days.

V/O
Fowzia Achmat moved to Bo Kaap with her family when they were forcibly removed from District Six.

Fowzia: District 6 and Bo Kaap has always been a sister community if I think of community spirit the very same spirit I came back here Its almost as if we came back to our roots because my great great great grandfather was a slave from Bengal India and my great great great grandmother was Sakie van der Kaap, so the very first mosque that was built was built by my great great great grandfather and my great great great grandmother donated the land for the mosque.

V/O
Auwal Mosque in Dorp Street is the oldest in South Africa…maybe not as old but as much part of Bo-Kaap is Atlas Trading Company, a family business for 46 years

V/O
Brothers, Wahab and Shouket Ahmed are at the helm of this spice emporium.

Wahab: We can walk anytime in night 12 o clock 1 o clock and there’s no problem because every body knows every body before we used to know if someone is sick there’s a death in the family every body used to get together and support the people it’s still going on but slowly dying.

Shouket: It was a very fantastic life the connection of the people the culture, the tradition that’s what we are afraid about outsiders moving in we like changes but change within what the history of the place.

Faldela: If my child …neighbour reprimand that’s what we are about haven for other children 10 15 children talking to each other plate of food open and giving we share we give its laughter my house is the haven for Bo Kaap …on my stoep

Ed: I love being here because I walk down the road and people go Hey Ed how I feel part of the community.

V/O
For Edmund February, Professor of Biological Sciences at the University of Cape Town, his Bo- Kaap childhood was without comparison.

Ed February: That’s what a neighbourhood is about its about going out there and knowing the people in your area and being able to relate to them and watching their kids growing up this what we are losing.

Link: Gentrification …in the Oxford Dictionary it’s defined as a process "renovating and improving a house or district so that it conforms to middle-class taste" But for residents here this means the desecration of their roots, the displacement of their families and the loss of their community.

Claire: What is the difference between gentrification or rejuvenation?
Ed February: If we were looking at rejuvenating the Bo- Kaap we would look at restoring it back to it’s former glory. Gentrification is funny word don’t like on some levels what some people see it as doing is upgrading the area I don’t believe that upgrading the area I think what that is it changes the whole ambience of area completely.

V/O
And with gentrification, the blanket value of properties rise, and so do rates and taxes making even the humblest house unaffordable for most working class residents.

Mohammad: My rates went up 400 % … no where in the world peoples rates went up by 400%.
/O 27 sec

In a Media statement , Cape Town's new Mayor, Dan Plato, has acknowledged the community's claims saying they had decided to initiate a public Participation process to provide the Bo-Kaap with the heritage protection it deserves .They regretted that this process had been delayed for so long. T he majority in council want to honour & protect the community’s heritage. The people of the Bo-Kaap deserve a speedy resolution to this matter.

V/O
The City of Cape Town declined to comment when we asked them for an interview in December last year. They said will be communicating, with the public about the proposed Heritage Protection Overlay Zone in due course.

Claire: Has the City failed the Bo Kaap area?
Ed February: Completely I don’t think the City has thought for one minute that this is a heritage area If they had thought about it they wouldn’t allow a 12 storey block of flats they wouldn’t be allowing the rates to keep climbing so that people can’t afford to live in the area and are being moved out.

Claire They are being squeezed out against their will?
Mohammad: So people somehow are being forced you either sell or you find other means of an income?.

V/O
The battle for the heart and soul of the Bo – Kaap community has gone on for long enough. With its centuries of heritage, a tourism mecca and melting pot of cultures, the time has come to put down a marker and protect Bo-Kaap for future generations.

Ed: The city should be thinking of the cultural heritage of the city they are the ones that should have some sort of vision of where they want to take their city and if they want to demolish the cultural heritage then that’s where the city is taking it.

Fazous I was once removed by forced removals I am not going to be moved this is where we are staying.

Mohammad: Bo Kaap remains still the most vibrant place if you go any where in the world book shop Bo kaap is cover or 3rd page attractive and
famous Bo kaap is in balance you going to lose when you lose Bo Kaap ….more than us all
